chunks: Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad al-Jawhari narrated from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah, who said:

I asked him about a man who anoints himself with oil containing perfume while intending to enter the state of ihram. He said: 'Do not anoint yourself with oil containing musk or ambergris, whose scent remains on your head after you enter ihram. And anoint yourself with whatever oil you wish when you intend to enter ihram, before and after the ritual bath. Once you have entered ihram, the oil becomes forbidden for you until you exit the state of ihram.'

key_terms.إِحْرَام: State of ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on using perfumed oil before and during ihram?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the juristic distinction between the scent of the oil itself and its residual fragrance, permitting perfumed oils before the ritual bath (Ghusl) but prohibiting them once the state of Ihram is formally entered. It highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on the continuity of the prohibition until the pilgrim performs the exit ritual (Hal), ensuring that the physical state of Ihram remains free from the specific impurity of musk and ambergris.
